title: Takht Akal Takht
hook: at Amritsar, the timeless throne founded by Guru Hargobind

segments.voice: Yesterday, the five in authority, from Anandpur and Chamkaur to the Akal Takht. Your line was five decide.

Late at night in Amritsar, after the last hymns, a palanquin is carried out of the Harmandir Sahib, across the causeway, through the courtyard, and up into the building that faces it. Inside rides the Guru Granth Sahib, going to rest for the night. In the early morning it comes back the same way, with singing. So every day the Guru travels between two buildings that look at each other across the courtyard. One stands in the water, low, with doors on every side. The other stands on land, raised, facing it.
screen: `A PALANQUIN CROSSES THE COURTYARD.` → `TWO BUILDINGS FACING EACH OTHER.` → `ONE IN THE WATER, ONE RAISED.`

segments.voice: You met the Akal Takht's two flags back in year one. Today, the building and its name. Akal means timeless, beyond death; Akal Purakh, the Timeless Being, is a Sikh name for God. Takht means a throne. So the name says the throne of the Timeless: not of a Guru, not of a ruler. The seat belongs to God, and whoever sits there sits on borrowed ground. Sikh tradition says Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, founded it at Amritsar, facing the Harmandir Sahib, and held court there: hearing the sangat, receiving offerings, settling the community's affairs. Tradition adds that he raised the platform with Baba Buddha and Bhai Gurdas, with their own hands. Now the shape of the place, which teaches without words. The Harmandir sits low, in the water, open on all sides, where the Guru's word is sung day and night. The Akal Takht stands on land, raised, looking straight at it, where the community's worldly matters are heard. Two kinds of work, and neither turned away from the other: decisions made in full view of the hymns. The Granth's night journey closes the loop. The word sung in the Harmandir by day rests at the Akal Takht by night. The Ardas remembers the five Takhts together, and the next days visit them one by one. Tradition counts the Akal Takht first among them, the one the Guru himself set up, the one the edicts go out from.
screen: `AKAL TAKHT: THE THRONE OF THE TIMELESS.` · `FOUNDED BY GURU HARGOBIND.` · `RAISED, FACING THE HARMANDIR.` · `THE GRANTH RESTS THERE BY NIGHT.` · then, large: `THE FIRST THRONE.`

segments.voice: See the courtyard at night, the water dark, the lights on the gold doubled underneath, and turn slowly in your mind between the two buildings, a few times: the place of song, the place of decision. Then let both stand together, facing each other, and rest there.
Takht Akal Takht. The throne of the Timeless at Amritsar, founded by Guru Hargobind, facing the Harmandir Sahib. Today's word.
Your line: the first throne. A seat that belongs to the Timeless, and to no one else. See you tomorrow.
